clue.text: Cold tea almost pleasant during breakfast, say

indicators.note: one set of pieces sits during, that is within, the meal word

parts.note: breakfast is an example of a meal
CHA is a British colloquial word for tea

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that their tea has gone cold while it was only nearly nice at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like it describes the tea but is the definition. 'almost' trims NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe behaviour done without feeling or warmth, automatic and unemotional.

clue.text: Fortune raised creates bad feeling

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: doom is one's fate or fortune

explanation.surface: A wealthy person's riches stir up resentment among others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fortune' suggests money, but here it means fate; 'raised' turns DOOM upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad mood is an ill temper, so a sulky or resentful feeling can be called a mood.

clue.text: Plant planted in choice land in England

indicators.note: the answer is planted inside, or set within, the run of words choice land in England

explanation.surface: A gardener sets a flower in prime English soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The lesser celandine is a small yellow-flowered spring wild flower, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Like good cold jelly?

parts.note: like means as
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A question about whether a well-made chilled jelly fits the description.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury gelatine made from meat stock, a clear jelly for coating cold dishes.

clue.text: Painter beginning to stucco entrance

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter

indicators.note: beginning to points at the first letter of the following word, stucco

explanation.surface: An artist starts plastering the doorway of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Ingres was a 19th-century French neoclassical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for going in, or the means of entry into a place.

clue.text: Sheet is one of these

parts.note: the letters of the word sheet rearranged spell these, so the word sheet is a rearrangement of the clue's last word

explanation.surface: Someone points at bedding and says it belongs to a group of linens.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: SHEET and THESE share the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another word's letters is called this, as sheet is from these.

clue.text: Detective's heading for criminal record

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, with the possessive S kept

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of the word criminal

explanation.surface: A police inspector goes off to look up someone's criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat disc, so the round object and the recording are the same.

clue.text: Riskier losing head getting more hostile

indicators.note: losing head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: dicier means riskier

explanation.surface: A situation gets more dangerous and nastier as leadership is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes the D from DICIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy reception is cold and unfriendly, so the comparative means more unwelcoming or frostier.

clue.text: Familiar rascal oddly hiding in nunnery

indicators.note: the selected letters are hiding in, or tucked inside, the word for a nunnery

parts.note: a nunnery is a convent

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of rascal

explanation.surface: A rogue has concealed himself among the nuns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar' here means knowledgeable, not friendly; 'oddly' picks the odd-numbered letters, which 'hiding in' sets inside the nunnery word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conversant with a subject means being acquainted or well versed in it.

clue.text: Deck ratings facing dock

parts.note: OR, other ranks, stands for ratings, non-officers in the forces
to dock is to cut off or lop

explanation.surface: Sailors face the harbour from the deck of their ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Possibly do a rating to find this?

definitions.text: Possibly do a rating to find this?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of do a rating can form another arrangement

explanation.surface: If you give something a rating, you might arrive at a graded scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: rating something places it on a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A grading step or a scale of successive stages is what results from ranking things.

clue.text: Poison scare in stews

indicators.note: stews means the letters of scare in are cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A food scare warning that toxins are in casseroles.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemical element is a notorious toxin used in classic murder mysteries.

clue.text: Amazingly Herculean lacking that man's kind of power

lacking says some letters are taken away from the mixed word

parts.note: that man is he

explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE from HERCULEAN and rearrange the remaining RCULEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic energy produced by fission is one type of power generation.

clue.text: Power rise certain to consume gallons

indicators.note: to consume means one word swallows, or holds inside, the other

parts.note: certain means sure

clue.text: Honourable guy has tried changing inside

indicators.note: changing means the letters of tried are rearranged

explanation.surface: A decent fellow has attempted to change his inner self.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' reads as a man but is a rope securing a tent or mast; 'changing' mixes the letters of tried before 'inside' puts them in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something creditable deserves praise, being worthy of respect and esteem.

clue.text: Exorbitant game's number one streetwise talent

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a game
I is the Roman numeral one
nous is practical good sense

explanation.surface: A sports star's natural ability is worth an outrageous fee.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS is British colloquial for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruinous costs so much that it could bankrupt you, so it is extortionate.

clue.text: Dismay of lover a website exposed

indicators.note: exposed means the run of letters is uncovered within lover a website

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that their partner has been revealed on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe someone is to intimidate or daunt them, filling them with fearful respect.

clue.text: Polite behaviour heard in country houses

indicators.note: heard signals that the word for country houses is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: manors are country houses of the landed gentry

explanation.surface: Good etiquette is noticed in stately homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Good social conduct and courtesy are called this, as in table etiquette.

clue.text: Labour always reportedly below target

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means this piece sits underneath the first

parts.note: a target or aim is an end

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: Workers are forever falling short of their goal.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the ending of the answer sounds like 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to toil or strive, so effort or work fits the word.

clue.text: Most mysterious bug seen by river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a bug is an insect pest

explanation.surface: An insect seen beside the water is the strangest yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee flows through Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep can mean obscure or hard to fathom, so the superlative is the most profound or enigmatic.

clue.text: Intro's changed round opening of Oliver Twist

indicators.note: round means the mixed letters go around the selected letter
changed means the letters of the clue word are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The start of Dickens's novel Oliver Twist has a reworked introduction.

explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the action of twisting, especially the strain on a twisted object.

clue.text: Master's expert teacher on ancient kingdom

indicators.note: on means the teacher word follows the previous pieces

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master
an ace is an expert
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster has a skilled tutor teaching about an ancient realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedon was the ancient Greek realm of Philip II and Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Good speed following motorway journey

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A trip goes well with a quick pace on the motorway.

explanation.definitionFit: To migrate is to travel from one region to another, as birds do seasonally.

clue.text: Bone's top part rotating

a bit is a part

clue.text: A block turned in wood

explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, used in models.

clue.text: Demure gal I allow to purchase special dress

clue.text: Many seeing love replaced by useless cravings

love is zero in tennis, the letter O
U/S is an abbreviation for unserviceable, useless

explanation.walkthrough: In LOTS the O is swapped for US.

clue.text: Take in text showing rising Queen hype

a long scarf or wrap worn by women over the shoulders

clue.text: Former husband with a male inspection

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
